title: KCET 2019 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: If $\sqrt[3]{y}\sqrt{x} = \sqrt[6]{(x+y)^5}$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$
questions.explanation: Taking logs and differentiating implicitly gives $y'(2x^2-3xy)=y(2x-3y)$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}$.

questions.q: Rolle's theorem is not applicable in which one of the following cases?
questions.explanation: $f(x)=|x|$ is not differentiable at $x=0\in(-2,2)$, so Rolle's theorem cannot be applied there.

questions.q: The interval in which the function $f(x)=x^3-6x^2+9x+10$ is increasing in
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=3(x-1)(x-3)\ge0$ for $x\le1$ or $x\ge3$, so $f$ is increasing on $(-\infty,1]\cup[3,\infty)$.

questions.q: The sides of an equilateral triangle are increasing at the rate of 4 cm/sec. The rate at which its area is increasing, when the side is 14 cm
questions.explanation: For side $s$, $A=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2$, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}s\dfrac{ds}{dt}$. With $s=14,\ ds/dt=4$ this gives $28\sqrt3$ cm$^2$/sec, which matches none of the printed options exactly (it equals $14\sqrt3$ only if $s=7$); KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The value of $\sqrt{24.99}$ is
questions.explanation: Using differentials, $\sqrt{25-0.01}\approx 5-\dfrac{0.01}{2\times5}=4.999$.

questions.q: If $|3x-5|\le 2$ then
questions.explanation: $-2\le 3x-5\le 2 \Rightarrow 3\le 3x\le 7 \Rightarrow 1\le x\le \dfrac{7}{3}$.

questions.q: A random variable X has the probability distribution $P(X=1)=k-1$, $P(X=2)=3k$, $P(X=3)=k$, $P(X=4)=3k$, $P(X=5)=3k^2$, $P(X=6)=k^2$, $P(X=7)=k^2+k$. Then the value of k is
questions.explanation: Summing all probabilities to 1 gives $5k^2+9k-2=0$, i.e. $(5k-1)(k+2)=0$, so $k=\dfrac{1}{5}$ (rejecting the negative root).

questions.q: If A and B are two events of a sample space S such that $P(A)=0.2$, $P(B)=0.6$ and $P(A|B)=0.5$ then $P(A'|B)=$
If X has a binomial distribution with parameters n = 6, p and P(X = 2) = 12, P(X = 3) = 5, then P =
questions.explanation: The printed values '12' and '5' do not give consistent probabilities, making the question ambiguous as printed; KEA awarded a grace mark. Taking the intended relation to give a symmetric distribution, $p=\dfrac{1}{2}$ is a reasonable value (as per KEA key).

questions.q: A man speaks truth 2 out of 3 times. He picks one of the natural numbers in the set $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$ and reports that it is even. The probability that it is actually even is
questions.explanation: By Bayes' theorem, $P(\text{even}\mid\text{reports even})=\dfrac{\frac37\cdot\frac23}{\frac37\cdot\frac23+\frac47\cdot\frac13}=\dfrac{6/21}{10/21}=\dfrac{3}{5}$.

questions.q: If U is the universal set with 100 elements; A and B are two sets such that $n(A)=50$, $n(B)=60$, $n(A\cap B)=20$ then $n(A'\cap B')=$
The domain of the function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2-7x+12}$ is
questions.explanation: We need $x^2-7x+12=(x-3)(x-4)\ge0$, true for $x\le3$ or $x\ge4$.

questions.q: If $\cos x = |\sin x|$ then the general solution is
questions.explanation: $\cos x=|\sin x|$ additionally requires $\cos x\ge0$; solving gives $x=2n\pi\pm\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, which alone keeps $\cos x$ non-negative.

questions.q: $\sqrt{3}\,\text{cosec}\,20^\circ - \sec 20^\circ =$
questions.explanation: Combining over a common denominator, $\sqrt3\cos20^\circ-\sin20^\circ=2\sin40^\circ$ and $\sin20^\circ\cos20^\circ=\tfrac12\sin40^\circ$, giving the value 4.

questions.q: If $P(n): 2^n < n!$, then the smallest positive integer for which $P(n)$ is true, is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Principle of Mathematical Induction
questions.explanation: Checking $n=1,2,3$ fails; at $n=4$, $2^4=16<24=4!$, so the smallest such integer is 4.

questions.q: Foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(1,3,4)$ to the plane $2x-y+z+3=0$ is
Acute angle between the line $\dfrac{x-5}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{-1}=\dfrac{z+4}{1}$ and the plane $3x-4y-z+5=0$ is
questions.explanation: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\cdot \vec n|}{|\vec a||\vec n|}=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{156}}$; writing $\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}$ simplifies to $\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{13}}$, giving $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{2\sqrt{13}}\right)$.

questions.q: The distance of the point $(1,2,1)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{1}=\dfrac{z-3}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: With a point on the line $(1,2,3)$ and direction $(2,1,2)$, the perpendicular distance is $\dfrac{|(0,0,-2)\times(2,1,2)|}{|(2,1,2)|}=\dfrac{2\sqrt5}{3}$.

questions.q: XY-plane divides the line joining the points $A(2,3,-5)$ and $B(-1,-2,-3)$ in the ratio
questions.explanation: The ratio is $-z_1:z_2 = 5:-3$; the negative sign shows the division is external, i.e. $5:3$ externally.

questions.q: The shaded region in the figure is the solution set of the inequations [figure: a triangular shaded region in the first quadrant, bounded above by the segment from (0,4) to (6,0), below by the segment from (0,3) to (10,0), and on the right by the vertical line x=6]
questions.explanation: Testing an interior point of the shaded triangle, e.g. $(5.5,0.5)$, satisfies $4x+5y\ge20$, $3x+10y\le30$ and $x\le6$.

questions.q: The order of the differential equation $y = C_1e^{C_2+x} + C_3e^{C_4+x}$ is
questions.explanation: $y=(C_1e^{C_2}+C_3e^{C_4})e^x=Ke^x$ has only one essential arbitrary constant, so the order is 1.

questions.q: If $|\vec a| = 16, |\vec b| = 4$ then $\sqrt{|\vec a \times \vec b|^2+|\vec a \cdot \vec b|^2} =$
questions.explanation: By the identity $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2+|\vec a\cdot\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2$, the required value is $\sqrt{|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2}=|\vec a||\vec b|=16\times4=64$.

questions.q: If the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ and the projection of $\vec a$ in the direction of $\vec b$ is $-2$, then $|\vec a| =$
questions.explanation: Projection $=|\vec a|\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=-\dfrac{|\vec a|}{2}=-2$, so $|\vec a|=4$.

questions.q: A unit vector perpendicular to the plane containing the vectors $\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$ and $-2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: The cross product of the two vectors is $(5,-5,5)$; normalising the opposite direction gives the unit vector $\dfrac{-\hat i+\hat j-\hat k}{\sqrt3}$.

questions.q: $[\vec a+2\vec b-\vec c,\ \vec a-\vec b,\ \vec a-\vec b-\vec c] =$
questions.explanation: Expanding the scalar triple product using the coefficient matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&2&-1\\1&-1&0\\1&-1&-1\end{pmatrix}$ gives determinant 3, so the result is $3[\vec a,\vec b,\vec c]$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3}\cot^{-1}x\,dx=$
questions.explanation: Since $\cot^{-1}x+\cot^{-1}(-x)=\pi$, the integral equals $\int_0^3\pi\,dx=3\pi$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt x + x\sqrt x}\,dx=$
questions.explanation: Substituting $t=\sqrt x$ gives $\int\dfrac{2}{1+t^2}\,dt=2\tan^{-1}\sqrt x+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x-1}{(x-1)(x+2)(x-3)}\,dx = A\log|x-1| + B\log|x+2| + C\log|x-3| + K$, then A, B, C are respectively
questions.explanation: By the cover-up rule, $A=\dfrac{-1}{6}$, $B=\dfrac{-1}{3}$, $C=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^2 [x^2]\,dx=$
questions.explanation: Splitting at $x=1,\sqrt2,\sqrt3$ where $[x^2]$ jumps, the integral evaluates to $(\sqrt2-1)+2(\sqrt3-\sqrt2)+3(2-\sqrt3)=5-\sqrt2-\sqrt3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sqrt{\dfrac{1+x}{1-x}}\,dx=$
questions.explanation: Writing the integrand as $\dfrac{1+x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, the antiderivative $\sin^{-1}x-\sqrt{1-x^2}$ evaluated from 0 to 1 gives $\dfrac{\pi}{2}+1$.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the equation $x^2+x+1=0$ then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta=-1,\ \alpha\beta=1$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=1-2=-1$.

questions.q: The number of 4 digit numbers without repetition that can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 in which each number has two odd digits and two even digits is
questions.explanation: Choose 2 of the 4 odd digits ($^4C_2=6$) and 2 of the 3 even digits ($^3C_2=3$), then arrange the 4 chosen digits in $4!=24$ ways: $6\times3\times24=432$.

questions.q: The number of terms in the expansion of $(x^2+y^2)^{25}-(x^2-y^2)^{25}$ after simplification is
questions.explanation: Only the odd-power terms in $y^2$ survive the subtraction, giving the 13 terms corresponding to odd $k=1,3,\dots,25$.

questions.q: The third term of a G.P. is 9. The product of its first five terms is
questions.explanation: The product of the first five terms equals $(ar^2)^5=9^5=3^{10}$.

questions.q: A line cuts off equal intercepts on the co-ordinate axes. The angle made by this line with the positive direction of X-axis is
questions.explanation: Equal intercepts give the line $x+y=a$, with slope $-1$, so the angle with the positive X-axis is $135^\circ$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int x^3\sin3x\,dx=$
questions.explanation: Repeated integration by parts on $x^3\sin3x$ gives option (C); differentiating it recovers $x^3\sin3x$, confirming the result.

questions.q: The area of the region above X-axis included between the parabola $y^2=x$ and the circle $x^2+y^2=2x$ in square units is
questions.explanation: For $0\le x\le1$ the circle lies above the parabola; the area between them is $\int_0^1\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}\,dx-\int_0^1\sqrt x\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-\dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.q: The area of the region bounded by Y-axis, $y=\cos x$ and $y=\sin x;\ 0\le x\le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=\pi/4$; the area is $\int_0^{\pi/4}(\cos x-\sin x)\,dx=[\sin x+\cos x]_0^{\pi/4}=\sqrt2-1$.

questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation $(2x+3y^2)\,dy = y\,dx\ (y>0)$ is
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dx}{dy}-\dfrac{2}{y}x=3y$ (linear in $x$), the integrating factor is $e^{\int -2/y\,dy}=y^{-2}$.

questions.q: The equation of the curve passing through the point (1, 1) such that the slope of the tangent at any point $(x,y)$ is equal to the product of its co-ordinates is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{y}=x\,dx\Rightarrow \ln y=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$; using $(1,1)$ gives $C=-\dfrac12$, i.e. $2\log y=x^2-1$.

questions.q: The eccentricity of the ellipse $9x^2+25y^2=225$ is
$\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^n (2r-1)=x$ then $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left[\dfrac{1^3+2^3+3^3+\cdots+n^3}{x^2}\right]=$
questions.explanation: $x=n^2$, and $\sum k^3=\dfrac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}\sim \dfrac{n^4}{4}$, so the limit is $\dfrac{n^4/4}{n^4}=\dfrac14$.

questions.q: The negation of the statement "All continuous functions are differentiable." is
options: All continuous functions are not differentiable.
Some continuous functions are not differentiable.
questions.explanation: The negation of a universal statement "All P are Q" is "Some P are not Q".

questions.q: Mean and standard deviation of 100 items are 50 and 4 respectively. The sum of all squares of the items is
questions.explanation: $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x^2}{n}-\bar x^2\Rightarrow \sum x^2=n(\sigma^2+\bar x^2)=100(16+2500)=251600$.

questions.q: Two letters are chosen from the letters of the word 'EQUATIONS'. The probability that one is vowel and the other is consonant is
questions.explanation: EQUATIONS has 5 vowels and 4 consonants among 9 letters; the required probability is $\dfrac{^5C_1\times{}^4C_1}{^9C_2}=\dfrac{20}{36}=\dfrac59$.

questions.q: The constant term in the expansion of $\begin{vmatrix}3x+1 & 2x-1 & x+2\\5x-1 & 3x+2 & x+1\\7x-2 & 3x+1 & 4x-1\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: The constant term is the value of the determinant at $x=0$, which works out to 6.

questions.q: If $[x]$ represents the greatest integer function and $f(x)=x-[x]-\cos x$ then $f'\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=$
questions.explanation: Away from integers, $[x]$ has zero derivative, so $f'(x)=1+\sin x$; at $x=\pi/2$, $f'=1+1=2$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin3x}{e^{2x}-1}$ for $x\ne0$ and $f(x)=k-2$ for $x=0$ is continuous at $x=0$, then $k=$
questions.explanation: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\sin3x}{e^{2x}-1}=\dfrac{3x}{2x}=\dfrac32$, so continuity needs $k-2=\dfrac32$, i.e. $k=\dfrac72$, which is not among the printed options; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question (as per KEA key).

questions.q: If $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left[\dfrac{2^{x+1}}{1+4^x}\right]$, then $f'(0)=$
questions.explanation: With $t=2^x$, $f(x)=2\tan^{-1}(2^x)$ for $x\le0$; $f'(x)=\dfrac{2\cdot2^x\ln2}{1+4^x}$, so $f'(0)=\dfrac{2\ln2}{2}=\log2$.

questions.q: If $x=a\sec^2\theta,\ y=a\tan^2\theta$ then $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=$
questions.explanation: Since $\sec^2\theta-\tan^2\theta=1$, $y=x-a$ is a straight line, so $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$.

questions.q: The inverse of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&5&0\\0&1&1\\-1&0&3\end{pmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: $|A|=1$; computing the cofactors and taking the adjugate gives the inverse shown in option (C).

questions.q: If P and Q are symmetric matrices of the same order then $PQ-QP$ is
questions.explanation: $(PQ-QP)'=Q'P'-P'Q'=QP-PQ=-(PQ-QP)$, so it is skew-symmetric.

questions.q: If $3A+4B'=\begin{pmatrix}7&-10&17\\0&6&31\end{pmatrix}$ and $2B-3A'=\begin{pmatrix}-1&18\\4&0\\-5&-7\end{pmatrix}$ then $B=$
questions.explanation: Transposing the second equation and adding it to the first eliminates $A$, giving $6B'=\begin{pmatrix}6&-6&12\\18&6&24\end{pmatrix}$, so $B'=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&2\\3&1&4\end{pmatrix}$ and hence $B$ as in option (A).

questions.q: If $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\4&2\end{pmatrix}, B=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, then $|ABB'|=$
If the value of a third order determinant is 16, then the value of the determinant formed by replacing each of its elements by its cofactor is
questions.explanation: For an $n\times n$ determinant $D$, the determinant of cofactors equals $D^{n-1}$; here $D^2=16^2=256$.

questions.q: $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $g:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=\sqrt x$. Which one of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: $g(-4)$ is not defined since $g$'s domain is $[0,\infty)$, so fog(-4) does not exist; hence statement (B) is not true.

questions.q: If $A=\{x\mid x\in\mathbb{N}, x\le5\}$, $B=\{x\mid x\in\mathbb{Z}, x^2-5x+6=0\}$, then the number of onto functions from A to B is
questions.explanation: $|A|=5,\ B=\{2,3\}$; the number of onto functions from a 5-element set to a 2-element set is $2^5-2=30$.

questions.q: On the set of positive rationals, a binary operation $*$ is defined by $a*b=\dfrac{2ab}{5}$. If $2*x=3^{-1}$ then $x=$
questions.explanation: The identity element for $*$ is $e=\dfrac52$; the inverse of 3 under $*$ satisfies $3*b=\dfrac52$, giving $b=\dfrac{25}{12}=3^{-1}$. Then $2*x=\dfrac{4x}{5}=\dfrac{25}{12}$ gives $x=\dfrac{125}{48}$.

questions.q: $\cos\left[2\sin^{-1}\dfrac34+\cos^{-1}\dfrac34\right]=$
questions.explanation: Since $\cos^{-1}\frac34=\frac{\pi}{2}-\sin^{-1}\frac34$, the bracket equals $\sin^{-1}\frac34+\frac{\pi}{2}$, and $\cos\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-\sin\theta=-\dfrac34$.

questions.q: If $a+\dfrac{\pi}{2}<2\tan^{-1}x+3\cot^{-1}x<b$ then 'a' and 'b' are respectively
questions.explanation: $2\tan^{-1}x+3\cot^{-1}x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}x$, whose range over all reals is $(\pi,2\pi)$; matching bounds gives $a+\pi/2=\pi\Rightarrow a=\pi/2$ and $b=2\pi$.
